lots.key_photo_findings: One photo, 3 rows x 8 = 24 boxed models in a carton. Left column and lower middle: 12 gold 'Limited Edition' boxes with Australian flag (Streets Ice Cream x2, Shell Motor Spirit No 108 x2, Coca-Cola x2, Cadbury's Dairy Milk x2, blue Arnott's-style van x2, Matchbox Series 'Est. 1953' yellow, plus a green cab-over 'Minties' truck that is NOT a Ford Model A, correcting the researcher). White and blue 'Special Collector's Model MB38 Ford Model A' boxes: The Australian x2, Weet-Bix x2, Arnott's Biscuits x2 (red), Matchbox Speed Shop. Two white Matchbox 'Matchbox Series' rosette boxes (yellow and green vans) and three blue-tartan Matchbox boxes with Australian flags: 'N.Z. Model Die Cast Club', 'Evening News', and a Model A with a figure panel. Old shop price stickers of $10, $15 and $10 on three boxes. Researcher mentioned Wests and Nestle; I could not see either.
lots.condition: Boxes look clean and complete with no obvious crushing; several window boxes show light shelf wear and price stickers. Models appear unplayed in boxes but were not seen out of the boxes; duplicates present.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are all 24 models present in their own boxes, any missing or broken windows, and are there any further models under the top layer?

lots.guide_summary: All sold evidence, no unsold or asking. Sum of parts from PriceCharting's eBay sold tables (US sales, single loose carts) at 1 USD = 1.4322 AUD: AUD 63 using the lowest sale inside 24 months for the 9 priced titles, to about AUD 112 using typical recent sales (Takahashi II US$18.95, Momotaro 11.50, Star Force 8.99, Baseball Star 8.99, DQ IV 8.63, DBZ 8.20, Xevious 5.50, Family Mahjong 5.00, Hole in One 2.09). Hottaman and Best Play Pro Yakyuu add only a few dollars and have no sale inside 24 months. These are single-cart prices; a mixed lot usually sells for less than the sum.
lots.working: SOLD singles inside 24 months, lowest each, USD: Xevious 1.75 + DQ IV 4.99 + DBZ Kyoushuu Saiyajin 5.20 + Star Force 8.99 + Family Mahjong 2.18 + Takahashi II 7.48 + Momotaro 8.21 + Baseball Star 3.92 + Hole in One 0.99 = US$43.71 x 1.4322 = AUD 62.60. Keep: 62.60 / 1.198 = 52.25, rounded down to $50. Flip: typical recent sales sum US$77.85 x 1.4322 = AUD 111.50; assume sold locally as a lot for about AUD 100 (10% bundle discount), less 13% eBay fees (AUD 13.00) and about AUD 12 outbound postage = AUD 75.00; 75.00 / 2.396 = 31.30, rounded down to $30. Adaptation: the lot is not sold as one item, prices are US eBay, so treat caps as soft. Gowans premium 19.8%; pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: All labels read in the photos and 9 titles have dated sold prices on opened pages, but the evidence is US single-cart sales via an aggregator rather than lot sales, and the carts are untested.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: DBZ Gekitou Tenkaichi Budoukai (pricecharting .../dragon-ball-z-gekitou-tenkaichi-budoukai): not in the lot (the second DBZ cart in photo 2 is the same Kyoushuu Saiyajin cart, not a 'DBZ2'), and its sales are Datach system bundles, a different item. Reclassified: the DQ IV US$8.36 and Xevious US$5.37 guide figures the researcher filed as ASKING are price-guide averages, not asks; replaced with real dated SOLD rows from the same pages. Corrected the researcher's assumed rate of 1.50 to 1.4322, the Pottermann reading to Hottaman no Chitei Tanken, and 'Best Baseball (SNK)' to Baseball Star.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows 11 carts with labels readable: Namcot 03 Xevious; ASCII HSP-11 Best Play Pro Yakyuu (1988); Hudson HFC-V7 Takahashi Meijin no Boukenjima II; Hudson Momotarou Densetsu (Peach Boy Legend, Chou series vol.3); USE Corporation USE-HC Hottaman no Chitei Tanken; Hudson HFC-SF Star Force; HAL-JO Jumbo Ozaki Hole in One Professional; SNK SFX-B9 Baseball Star Mezase Sankanou; Namcot Family Mahjong; Bandai Dragon Ball Z Kyoushuu! Saiyajin; Enix EFC-D4 Dragon Quest IV (1990). Photo 2 shows the same carts stacked in a small box (DBZ on top, DQ IV in front), so there is no extra DBZ cart and probably no hidden extras.
lots.condition: Loose carts, no boxes or manuals, untested. Labels mostly intact with light wear; Momotaro shell yellowed; Hole in One label slightly scuffed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is it just the 11 carts shown in photo 1, or are there more carts in the box? Any label damage or cracked shells?

lots.what_it_is: Framed hand-coloured engraved chart 'Carte de la Terre Van-Diemen' with inset 'Plan de la Baie de l'Aventure', from the French edition of Cook's third voyage (Paris, about 1785), by Bonne; originality not confirmed
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher found nothing and my WebSearch calls were refused (shared search budget used up), and Invaluable's search page loads results client-side so I could not read them without a search. The scanner's $120-300 framed figure is not evidence. A follow-up search session is needed before bidding on value.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Gowans premium 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198); pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Plate marks read but originality (period engraving versus a modern facsimile) cannot be judged from one photo through glass, and there is no price evidence.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (the researcher submitted no entries).
lots.key_photo_findings: Cropped and enlarged the margins: top left reads 'Cook. 3e Voyage', top centre 'Longitude Est de Paris', plate number at top right (looks like 33 or 35), bottom left signature faint (looks like 'Benard ... direx.'), bottom right faint engraver credit ('... sculp.'). Title cartouche 'Carte de la Terre Van-Diemen, Par M. Bonne, Ingenieur-Hydrographe de la Marine'. Inset 'Plan de la Baye de l'Aventure sur la Terre Van-Diemen'. Coast hand-coloured yellow, red and blue compass rose. This places it in the atlas to the French edition of Cook's third voyage, not the Encyclopedie Methodique as the researcher suggested. Burr-veneer frame, cream mount with gold slip, under glass. Gowans title: 'VAN DIEMEN - ADVENTURE BAY MAP', 3 bids already on 7 Oct.
lots.condition: Sheet looks clean and bright with no visible foxing or stains through the glass; colour looks fresh, which could mean later colouring or a facsimile. Plate mark not visible under the mount.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is it an original copper engraving on laid paper (plate mark and chain lines visible if unframed or from the back) or a modern print? Any foxing, trimming or repairs, and is there a framer's or dealer's label on the back?
